matches.note: FASTNET ROCK. It is printed on p.51 under the Scottish West Coast running head, but the position is Irish.
KINSALE OLD HEAD. Not row 367, which is the Kinsale Harbour light at Fort Charles.
Findlay's 'Dungarvan' entry describes a 'White tower ... on Ballinacourty Pt.'
Findlay prints HOOK POINT.
Findlay calls it SALTEES LT.-VESSEL, 'off Coningbeg Rock'. It is the only light-vessel between Hook and the Barrels.
The reports once print 'Tuskar Rock Lt.-ship', but Tuskar is a lighthouse (circular tower) and Findlay has no light-vessel of that name.
Part 1 of the row is the head light. Part 2 is the pier light, which is not the station.
KISH LIGHTVESSEL. The reports' 'Kirk Bank' is a misprint.
Findlay prints HOWTH-BAILEY. Not row 398, which is Howth Harbour.
SOUTH ROCK LT.-VES, which 'supersedes S. Rock lt.-ho.'

Findlay 1887 lists only MEW ISLAND, established 1884. The reports print 'Copeland Island' from 1881. For 1881-1883 the observer was probably at the old Copeland light on Lighthouse Island, about a mile away, which had a different character. Row 410's position and character apply from 1884 only.
MAIDENS: one row for two towers 800 yds apart. The row is shared with maidens-south.
Shares row 413 with maidens-north.
RATHLIN light, on Altacarry (N.E.) point.
Findlay prints INNISTRAHULL.
The reports print 'Lough Swilly'. Findlay has FANNET POINT, the Lough Swilly entrance light. It falls between Dunree/Buncrana and Tory, which matches the coast order.

The reports print 'Killybegs', and Findlay has a separate entry named 'Killybegs' (row 427). That entry is St. John Point light (54 34.1N, 8 27.6W), not Rotten Island. I matched row 428 (Rotten Island, 54 36.8N 8 26.4W) because the station id says Rotten Island. If the observer was actually at St. John Point, use row 427.
One row covers both leading lights ('Two fixed bright lights'). The row has no character or longitude in those fields; the character is in the description.
EAGLE ISLAND: one row for two towers 132 yds apart. The row is shared with eagle-island-west.
Shares row 433 with eagle-island-east.
BLACK ROCK at 54 4.2N 10 19.3W, between Eagle Island and Black Sod. Not row 429, which is the Sligo Black Rock (54 18N, 8 37W).
Findlay's 'Black Sod Quay' is a 'House on Black Sod Point'.
SLYNE HEAD: one row for two towers. The N. light is revolving, the S. fixed. The row is shared with slyne-head-south.
Shares row 437 with slyne-head-north. This is the fixed light.
EERAGH ISLAND, the North Aran light.
Inisheer Island, the South Aran light. The reports once print 'Straw Island, S.', which is a slip.
Findlay's 'Tralee' entry is the light 'On Little Samphire Island'.
TEARAGHT ISLAND.
CALF ROCK. The lighthouse was destroyed in the gale of 26 Nov 1881, and the station is reported for 1881 only.

Findlay has no separate Dursey entry. Row 451 (Calf Rock) says a temporary light 'of same character is shown from lt.-ho. on S.W. extr. o[f Dursey Island]'; the transcription is cut off there. Dursey replaces Calf Rock in the reports from 1882, which fits. But row 451's position is for Calf Rock, not the light on Dursey.

notes: Things to check: (1) rotten-island: the reports print 'Killybegs', which is also Findlay's name for St. John Point (row 427), while row 428 is Rotten Island. Confirm which light the keeper was at. (2) copeland: Findlay 1887 has only Mew Island (est. 1884). For the 1881-83 reports the old Copeland (Lighthouse Island) light's position and character are probably needed from another source. (3) dursey-island: matched to the Calf Rock row (451) through its temporary-light note, which is cut off in the transcription. Check the full text, and note that the position printed is Calf Rock's. (4) Rows covering two stations: 413 (Maidens N/S), 433 (Eagle Island E/W) and 437 (Slyne Head N/S). Oyster Island's two leading lights are also a single row (430). Each of these rows gives one position for both lights. (5) Name differences: SALTEES LT.-VESSEL is Coningbeg, Tralee is Samphire Island, Dungarvan is Ballinacourty, FANNET POINT is Lough Swilly, Black Sod Quay is Blacksod Point, HOOK POINT is Hook Tower. (6) Two Black Rocks: row 434 is Mayo, row 429 is Sligo. (7) Possible transcription or parsing problems: row 416 (Inishowen) has latitude 53 13.6, surely a slip for 55 (it doesn't affect any match); row 437's year field reads '1836 / null'; row 433 has no year; row 430 has no character or longitude. Fastnet, Galley Head and Old Head (rows 364-366) sit under the 'SCOTLAND; IRELAND, West Coast' running head on p.51. No station is left without a match.
